title: Check yourself: JVM tuning and monitoring

questions.stem: An inventory service runs with -Xmx4g. `jcmd <pid> GC.heap_info` shows used 3,300,000K at 10:00 and 3,500,000K at 10:05. A colleague calls it a leak and wants to run `jcmd <pid> GC.class_histogram` on the production instance right away. What do you suggest?

options.text: Run the plain histogram now, since it only reads the heap and stops nothing
options.says: a plain class histogram runs a stop-the-world full collection before it counts

options.text: Run the plain histogram now, since used counts only live objects and its growth is the leak
options.says: used counts every byte in the regions handed out, garbage included, so its growth shows no leak

options.text: Watch the heap left after each full collection, since used also counts garbage no collection has emptied
options.says: used includes garbage until a collection empties it; a leak is the heap after full collections climbing, and the plain histogram would force a full GC

options.text: Watch the heap left after each full collection, since the plain histogram counts garbage as well as live objects
options.says: the plain histogram counts only live objects, which is why it runs a full collection first; -all is the one that counts garbage

origin.section: GC.heap_info Counts Garbage as Used; Live Data Is What a Full Collection Leaves

questions.stem: A service hangs. `jcmd <pid> Thread.print` has no deadlock section. Thirty request threads are BLOCKED at `- waiting to lock <0x00000006c1d2a3c0> (a com.shop.RateCache)`. The thread `rate-refresher` is RUNNABLE in `sun.nio.ch.NioSocketImpl.read`, and further down its stack, under `RateCache.refresh`, has `- locked <0x00000006c1d2a3c0> (a com.shop.RateCache)`. What is going on?

options.text: The requests wait for the socket read to end, since rate-refresher keeps the cache's monitor while it reads
options.says: the - locked line under refresh is the monitor the requests wait for, and the thread is still inside that synchronized code, in a read

options.text: The requests wait for something besides the socket read, since rate-refresher gave up the cache's monitor when its read started
options.says: only Object.wait releases a monitor while the thread waits; a blocking read keeps every monitor the thread holds

options.text: The requests are in a deadlock with rate-refresher, since the dump leaves out cycles that involve monitors
options.says: Thread.print reports cycles of monitors (and of ReentrantLocks), and here there is no cycle: rate-refresher waits for a socket, not a lock

options.text: The requests will get through one by one, since a dump with no deadlock section means the monitor is passed on
options.says: no deadlock section only means no cycle of locks; the holder can wait forever on something else, and every blocked thread waits with it

origin.section: A Thread Dump Names a Deadlock Cycle, Not a Thread Stuck Behind a Holder That Waits

questions.stem: A team replaced the synchronized methods of its OrderBook with a ReentrantLock. Throughput did not change. A new recording with the default settings has no jdk.JavaMonitorEnter events for OrderBook. What can the team conclude?

options.text: The order book no longer causes waits, since a thread that can't get a ReentrantLock spins instead of parking
options.says: a thread that can't get a ReentrantLock parks; the recording shows those waits as jdk.ThreadPark events

options.text: The order book no longer causes waits, since a wait for any lock type is recorded as jdk.JavaMonitorEnter
options.says: jdk.JavaMonitorEnter covers only synchronized monitors; a ReentrantLock wait is a jdk.ThreadPark event

options.text: The order book may still cause waits, since a wait for a ReentrantLock is recorded as jdk.ThreadPark
options.says: the same ledger with a ReentrantLock recorded no jdk.JavaMonitorEnter events, and its waits were jdk.ThreadPark events naming ReentrantLock$NonfairSync

options.text: The order book may still cause waits, since the default settings drop lock waits longer than 20 ms
options.says: the threshold works the other way: the default settings drop waits shorter than 20 ms and record the longer ones

origin.section: JFR Lock Events Name the Lock, the Waiter and the Previous Owner, Above a Threshold

questions.stem: A pricing service starts with no heap flags on Java 21, in a container whose memory limit is 2 GB, on a node with 64 GB. What maximum heap does the JVM choose?

options.text: About 16 GB, since the JVM takes a quarter of the node's memory
options.says: with container support, on by default, the JVM sizes the heap from the container's limit, not the node's memory

options.text: About 512 MB, since the JVM takes a quarter of the container's limit
options.says: MaxRAMPercentage defaults to 25, applied to the memory the JVM sees, which in a container is its limit

options.text: About 1.5 GB, since the JVM leaves a quarter of the limit for memory outside the heap
options.says: the default share is 25 %; 75 % takes -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75

options.text: About 2 GB, since the JVM leaves it to the limit to stop the heap from growing
options.says: the JVM fixes a maximum heap at startup; without -Xmx it is 25 % of the memory it sees

origin.section: Without -Xmx the Heap Is a Quarter of the Memory the JVM Sees

questions.stem: A gateway runs with -Xmx3g in a container limited to 4 GB. Under load it is restarted as OOMKilled. Its GC log shows the heap after each collection below 2 GB, and its log has no OutOfMemoryError. What happened?

options.text: The process went over the limit with memory outside the heap, since the limit counts the memory of the whole process
options.says: stacks, compiled code, the collector's structures and direct buffers live outside the heap, the kernel charges the pages they touch to the container, and it kills the process without a Java error

options.text: The process went over the limit with heap beyond -Xmx, since -Xmx caps only the heap that remains after a collection
options.says: -Xmx caps the heap at every moment; the memory beyond it is outside the heap

options.text: The kernel counted memory the JVM had only reserved, since a container limit applies to the address space a process reserves
options.says: reserved address space costs nothing; the container is charged for pages the process touches

options.text: The kernel counted the whole -Xmx from the start, since the JVM commits its maximum heap as soon as it starts
options.says: without -Xms the JVM starts with a small initial heap (1/64 of the memory) and commits more only as the heap grows

origin.section: The Process Is Bigger Than the Heap
